In 1901, British humanitarian Emily Hobhouse visited the concentration camps of the Boer War and was horrified by what she discovered. Starving children, disease, and appalling living conditions were claiming thousands of lives. Her shocking report exposed the suffering of women and children, sparking public outrage and a government investigation.
